text:
Caroline: Hey team — CaroTech started seeing a spike of 429s from prod-eu for our streaming chat flows yesterday ~18:30 UTC. Only happens for long-lived sessions (sessions > ~2m). 429 body shows "Retry-After: 30". Affected user: acct-ct-123. Sample request id: req_20260317_az1_xyz. Anyone seen this pattern? cc @Maya

Maya: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK trace) and the SDK version? Also roughly how many concurrent sessions/users and RPM/TPM you expect?

Caroline: Repro attached below. We use the JS streaming SDK v0.9.5. Typical steady-state: ~120 concurrent sessions from a single instance, each session sends a tiny keepalive every 5s to keep WS alive. When session goes long (>2m) we start seeing 429s. We tried increasing client retry, but retries just make it worse.

Caroline: ```bash
# simplified repro (Websocket keepalive via REST ping)
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"session_id":"s-123","prompt":"ping","stream":true}'
```

Ethan: Thanks. From the symptom set this looks like a per-tenant TPM window being hit (many small requests -> tokens-per-minute limit). Can you share the response headers from a failed request (we log X-Redwood-* headers)? Also do you have the X-Request-ID from the failing responses?

Caroline: One failing response header dump from last night: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 18:42:12 GMT
X-Redwood-Ratelimit-Limit: 6000
X-Redwood-Ratelimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Ratelimit-Reset: 208
Retry-After: 30
X-Request-ID: req_20260317_az1_xyz
```

Maya: X-Redwood-Ratelimit-Limit 6000 — is that tokens per minute or tokens per 5m? Platform teams: clarify. @Priya

Priya: That header is tokens-per-minute (TPM) for the tenant rate window. Looks like their small keepalive pings generate many requests with low token counts, but we count tokens for each request — net effect is high TPM. Because the limit is per-tenant, a single noisy instance can exhaust it.

Ethan: Quick mitigation options:
- Customer: increase keepalive interval (e.g., 30s+) or switch to a single session-level heartbeat instead of frequent REST pings.
- Support: apply temporary quota bump/override for acct-ct-123 while they adjust client behavior.
- Platform: consider adding an ingress smoothing rule to aggregate small pings by session_id for rate accounting.

Maya: Caroline — can you try disabling the 5s keepalive (or set to 30s) in a canary environment and let us know if 429s stop? If you want a faster unblock we can do a +2x temporary TPM for 2 hours — need account owner approval.

Caroline: Can confirm: I changed keepalive from 5s -> 35s on a subset (10 sessions) and those sessions stopped hitting 429s within 10 minutes. The other sessions still hit 429s.

Ethan: Good repro. I'll open a temporary override. @Priya — any concerns raising TPM for this tenant short-term? We should also add a dashboard panel to show small-request fraction vs tokens.

Priya: Ok to grant a short override (+2x TPM for 2 hours) while they fix client. Also raising a platform task to evaluate grouping small heartbeats into a single accounting event. I'll create a ticket: PLAT-5489.

Maya: Created support ticket and temporary override. Ticket: SUP-2026-334, override id ov-ct-20260317-1. ETA: override active in ~15m. Please test after that.

rl-bot: deploy-notify: temporary quota override ov-ct-20260317-1 applied to acct-ct-123 by maya (support). Duration: 2h.

Caroline: Received the override, re-tested with full fleet — 429 rate dropped to near-zero for the next 20m. Thanks. We'll land client change to 30s+ keepalive and release SDK patch.

Ethan: Follow-ups I will do:
- Add a per-tenant TPM vs small-request ratio dashboard (Grafana) and alert if >30% small-request tokens (ticket PLAT-5490).
- Propose an ingress rule to group requests < 3 tokens within a rolling 10s window by session_id (architecture doc PR incoming).

Maya: Guidance for customers (we'll add to KB):
1) Prefer batching/longer keepalives; avoid 5s polling.
2) Honor Retry-After header and exponential backoff in SDKs.
3) If you must do frequent tiny pings, ask support for a quota review.

Caroline: Super helpful — thanks all. We'll roll SDK patch tomorrow and follow up on SUP-2026-334 when the change is live. :thumbsup:

Maya: Closing loop — marking ticket SUP-2026-334 as resolved after customer confirms SDK release. If anything reappears reopen.

Caroline: Confirmed fixed after SDK v0.9.6 with 30s heartbeat. No further 429s for 48h. Closing from our side.
